posts.text:
Today’s controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant demonstrates the power of a coordinated, whole-of-government response. Initial assessments indicate that measures to contain the blast and limit the spread of lead dust exceeded expectations, and real-time air monitors are reporting no detectable airborne lead.

I thank President Trump and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller for their leadership in coordinating federal resources to protect surrounding communities. 

The @USArmy, @EPA, @FEMA, @USDA, @ATFHQ, @HHSGov, and state and local partners coordinated the controlled detonation and continue working together to assess and address potential health risks.

I especially thank @ASPRgov Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary Sean Kaufman, @CDCgov Director Dr. Erica Schwartz, and every HHS employee who deployed to Iowa to protect residents’ health and safety.

ASPR deployed nine staff ahead of the detonation—seven to Iowa and two to FEMA’s regional coordination center in Kansas City. They continue to coordinate federal health and medical resources, assess state and local behavioral health needs and response capabilities, and represent HHS in response planning.

Approximately 80 CDC and ATSDR personnel have supported the response, including liaison officers in Iowa and Kansas City. Working with state and federal partners, their teams are coordinating community health assessments, reviewing environmental data, and helping answer residents’ questions about lead exposure and blood lead testing.

I also thank @FDA’s human foods and veterinary medicine teams for providing technical expertise and answering questions about potential risks to the human food supply and animal feed.

Our responsibility does not end with the detonation. We will continue working with Iowa officials and our federal partners to assess potential health risks, share findings, and respond to residents’ needs. Iowa families deserve clear answers about what the monitoring shows, what remains under investigation, and what they should do to protect their health.
